page: Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-200s-amd is an AMD-based instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features a memory-optimized allocation pattern with an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, delivering 32.0 GB of RAM alongside 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The processor architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, backed by vector and cryptographic hardware instruction sets including AVX-512 (f, vnni, bf16), AES, and SHA_NI. The instance includes 200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, one complimentary public IPv4 address, and operates without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core and memory performance. The instance achieved 3434.57 in stress-ng single-core tests, placing it in the top 10% of tested systems, paired with a Geekbench single-core score of 2149.0. Memory throughput is also competitive, with PassMark memory scoring in the top 25% and large-block uncached write bandwidth measuring 113.08 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded capacity remains bounded by the 4 vCPU topology, showing mid-tier multi-core stress-ng (13688.52) and Geekbench (6690.0) metrics, along with bottom-quartile throughput for static web serving (3.81 GB/sec) and PassMark database operations.

Given its high memory density per compute unit and fast local NVMe storage, this configuration offers solid cost efficiency for memory-heavy single-threaded tasks, in-memory data structures, caching layers like Redis (demonstrating 10.61 million SET ops/sec), and batch compression jobs. It is less suitable for high-concurrency multi-threaded web servers or large-scale language model inference due to its limited vCPU count and lack of accelerator hardware.
description: The Vultr voc-m-4c-32gb-200s-amd is a memory-oriented server in the Optimized Cloud Compute lineup, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical AMD EPYC cores at 2.0 GHz) and 32.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Built on x86_64 architecture with 32 MB L3 cache and AVX-512 support, the node includes 200 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and one public IPv4 address, without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, ranking in the top 10% for single-core stress-ng tests, alongside top-quartile memory bandwidth and compression speeds. However, multi-core throughput and high-concurrency database operations remain constrained by the low core count. This instance is best suited for memory-intensive caching tiers, single-threaded processing pipelines, and in-memory analytical workloads requiring substantial RAM per core.
